test: Join bill lines to PO lines on po_id+sku; compute line excess = max(0, billed qty*cost - PO qty*PO cost) for bills paid in full (payment = bill amount). Break down by year, vendor, SKU; check whether higher unit costs persist after first appearance per vendor/SKU (step change = agreed price increase) or are one-off scattered; check whether later bills/POs for the same SKU revert to PO cost; check vendor credits per vendor against excess; compare paid-in-full vs short-paid groups.
support: Excess >= $0.2M every year, spread across vendors, unit-cost excess is sporadic per vendor-SKU (next bill reverts to PO cost, so not a price step), vendor credits too small to offset, and paid-in-full vs short-paid bills indistinguishable on vendor/size/ratio.
weaken: Overbilled unit costs concentrate in persistent runs per vendor-SKU (consistent with an un-updated PO price), or vendor credits per vendor approximate the excess, or excess is under $0.2M in many years.
expect: Strongly expect support: standard cost never changes so PO cost is fixed; a price increase would appear as all subsequent bills higher, which I expect not to see (ratio ~1.05 scattered). Expect ~$0.3M/yr line excess, vendor credits ~$0.19M/yr total and not related. Confidence ~75%.
